_note: How much research each run does. Research runs every 15 minutes and starts as many researchers as the queue needs, up to sweep.researchers (the cap on usage); an empty queue starts none. Gap searchers: sweep.gap_workers every sweep.gap_every_minutes, plus sweep.gap_spare_workers while the 5-hour usage window is under sweep.gap_spare_below_pct of its estimate, none when usage is tight (measured 2026-11-19/20: 122 gap runs added 11 events, 91% added nothing, $3.58 per event against $0.95 for a researcher). The backlog desk only acts when more than backlog.leave_for_sweep stories are waiting. The editor job may move these by at most a quarter a week; the owner can set them to anything. headless true (owner, 2026-11-19): every AI job runs as one scripts/run-job.mjs call in swarm phases (plan, claim leases, work, check, retry, commit, report); a job whose workers cannot read the web here falls back to subagents. sweep.review_workers: every research run also starts up to this many reviewers on the oldest unreviewed events (continuous second review); the hourly review desk catches the rest. flow: research is one continuous loop (run-job.mjs flow): collect, research new stories and review earlier events in parallel, commit, repeat every min_cycle_minutes or as soon as a cycle ends; it lives `minutes` and the research schedules restart it. flow.update_workers: each cycle also starts up to this many updaters on published events with new reporting (scripts/updates.mjs); flow.followup_every_minutes: how often the loop also runs the follow-up desk on developing and claimed events. flow.grid_workers / flow.grid_per_worker: each cycle also runs scripts/grid.mjs collect, then starts up to grid_workers grid researchers (role grid) on the biggest grid outages that need a cause, grid_per_worker incidents each (scripts/grid-desk.mjs plan and apply; 0 turns it off). flow.idle_backoff_minutes: how long the loop waits after 0, 1, 2+ idle cycles in a row; collection keeps min_cycle_minutes during a longer wait and work found starts the next cycle at once. usage_budget: see its own _note (scripts/lib/usage.mjs).

usage_budget._note: The Max plan has no dollar limit but a 5-hour and a weekly usage window, and it does not publish them. These are estimates (scripts/lib/usage.mjs reads data/usage/*.jsonl, headless workers only; the ops and interactive sessions use the same plan and are not counted, so keep a margin). Derived 2026-11-20 from 26.6 hours of the usage log (2026-11-19 04:35 to 11-20 07:13), no limit hit in that time: peak rolling 5 hours 86.0 M tokens and $40.05 (19 Nov 17:47 to 22:47, while two loops ran at once), x 1.5 = window_tokens and window_cost. The log holds less than a week, so the weekly figures are the peak rolling 24 hours (319.1 M tokens, $152.25) x 7 x 1.5. Levels: tight at tight_pct of either window (the loop runs only researchers on incidents and exploited flaws and reviewers past 20 minutes; the jobs in tight_skip_jobs wait), stop at stop_pct of the 5-hour window or on a real limit hit (no workers until the reset time the error gives, else limit_backoff_minutes). The weekly estimate never stops the loop by itself. Re-derive these once a full week of the log exists (node scripts/lib/usage.mjs prints the current level and the peaks).
